doc.title: Lou Pallo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007

title: Cramping hands
summary: Pallo describes finger cramping over the past two years and arthritis among Bucky and Les.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Have you ever had any physical ailments from years and years of that?

Yes. Yes. Lately, the past two years I would say, where a finger, everything just cramps and I can’t move them. It’s not arthritis, I guess maybe from all the years. And even the pick hand, I’ll be playing like this and all of a sudden this finger will go out like that and I can’t control it. And I have to stop and try to do this. And like Bucky has the arthritis, Les has it, everyone has arthritis. I don’t actually have bad arthritis but they do cramp and they get into a fixed position and I can’t move them.
Well you think of how many hours those hands spend doing that.
Years and years of playing, Right. And here I thought it would be better because you’re always using them. It should be helping.
